title: Pasting canonical pro-etale derived pullback comparisons for factored endomorphisms
statement:
Let $u:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Use $D_T=D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A_T)$ for $T=X,Y$, the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and derived module pullbacks [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The constant ring sheaves and their identifications $v^{-1}A_{\mathrm{target}(v)}\cong A_{\mathrm{source}(v)}$ are the canonical ones of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], with their composite identification as in [lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition]. Write $P_v=Lv^*$ and $c_{h,k}:P_{k\circ h}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_hP_k$ for the K-flat-normalized comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition].

For $T=X,Y$ let $r_T,s_T:T\to T$ be endomorphisms satisfying $ur_X=r_Yu$ and $us_X=s_Yu$. Put $t_T=s_T\circ r_T$, so $ut_X=t_Yu$, and $d_T=c_{r_T,s_T}:P_{t_T}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{r_T}P_{s_T}$. For $v=r,s,t$, define the commuting-square comparison
$$
 C_v:P_uP_{v_Y}\xrightarrow{c_{u,v_Y}^{-1}}P_{v_Yu}
 =P_{uv_X}\xrightarrow{c_{v_X,u}}P_{v_X}P_u.
$$
The middle arrow is transport along the given equality of scheme morphisms; all functor associators are understood. Then, as natural transformations $D_Y\to D_X$,
$$
 (P_{r_X}C_s)\circ(C_rP_{s_Y})\circ(P_ud_Y)
 =(d_XP_u)\circ C_t:
 P_uP_{t_Y}\longrightarrow P_{r_X}P_{s_X}P_u.
$$
The equality holds for the specified canonical comparisons, including their transports along morphism equalities. Their components on any K-flat complex of $A_Y$-modules with flat terms are the classes of the corresponding termwise module-pullback pasting maps. No Cartesian-square, smoothness, finite-type, or invertibility hypothesis on $u,r_T,s_T$ is imposed.

proof.text: Use [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] to regard every arrow in the two squares as a morphism of ringed pro-etale topoi with its specified constant-section coefficient map. By [lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition], the coefficient map for any composite is exactly the successive coefficient map. Consequently [lem-trf-derived-pullback-coherence] applies with the very comparisons $c$ in the item, rather than with newly chosen composition isomorphisms. We will apply its displayed equation to the three composable triples $(u,r_Y,s_Y)$, $(r_X,u,s_Y)$, and $(r_X,s_X,u)$. Each triple consists of morphisms of schemes with the same finite commutative ring $A$; no geometric property of those morphisms is required.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; agent pasting deduction from the normalized associativity statement lem-trf-derived-pullback-coherence

proof.text:
Here is the convention for every equality transport in the calculation. For an equality $e:a=b$ of parallel scheme arrows write $E(e):P_a\to P_b$ for its induced natural isomorphism. For $e:b=b'$ and $q:a=a'$ the composition comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] satisfy
$$(P_aE(e))c_{a,b}=c_{a,b'}E(e\circ a),\qquad (E(q)P_b)c_{a,b}=c_{a',b}E(b\circ q).$$
These are substitution in the two indices of the specified family $c$: eliminating the equality makes both sides identical. Likewise $E(e'e)=E(e')E(e)$, inverse equalities give inverse transports, and whiskering gives the corresponding transport of composed functors. The equality defining the outer square can be taken to be
$$(s_Yr_Y)u=s_Y(r_Yu)=s_Y(ur_X)=(s_Yu)r_X=(us_X)r_X=u(s_Xr_X).$$
Any other given proof of this same equality induces the same transport, since equality proofs are propositions. In steps 3--5 we write the formulas after these substitutions, suppressing $E$ and retaining the canonical functor associators. The two displayed substitution identities specify how to insert every suppressed transport. This is an elementary equality calculation, not an extra pseudofunctor coherence hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; agent pasting deduction from the normalized associativity statement lem-trf-derived-pullback-coherence

proof.text:
Let $H=(P_{r_X}C_s)(C_rP_{s_Y})(P_ud_Y)$. Apply [lem-trf-derived-pullback-coherence] to $(j,h,k)=(u,r_Y,s_Y)$:
$$(P_ud_Y)c_{u,t_Y}=(c_{u,r_Y}P_{s_Y})c_{r_Yu,s_Y}.$$
Right-compose with $c_{u,t_Y}^{-1}$ and substitute into $H$. Expand $C_r=c_{r_X,u}c_{u,r_Y}^{-1}$ with the transport of step 2. The adjacent factors $c_{u,r_Y}^{-1}P_{s_Y}$ and $c_{u,r_Y}P_{s_Y}$ cancel. Substitution along $r_Yu=ur_X$ therefore gives
$$H=(P_{r_X}C_s)(c_{r_X,u}P_{s_Y})c_{ur_X,s_Y}c_{u,t_Y}^{-1}.$$
All equations are equations of natural transformations; the use of the coherence statement componentwise at every input object gives that equation of transformations by extensionality.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; agent pasting deduction from the normalized associativity statement lem-trf-derived-pullback-coherence

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-derived-pullback-coherence] to $(j,h,k)=(r_X,u,s_Y)$:
$$(c_{r_X,u}P_{s_Y})c_{ur_X,s_Y}=(P_{r_X}c_{u,s_Y})c_{r_X,s_Yu}.$$
Insert this equality into step 3. Expanding $C_s=c_{s_X,u}c_{u,s_Y}^{-1}$ cancels $P_{r_X}c_{u,s_Y}^{-1}$ against $P_{r_X}c_{u,s_Y}$, by functoriality of $P_{r_X}$. Substitute $s_Yu=us_X$ with the transport convention of step 2. We obtain
$$H=(P_{r_X}c_{s_X,u})c_{r_X,us_X}c_{u,t_Y}^{-1}.$$
This uses the second square only to identify its two composite scheme arrows.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; agent pasting deduction from the normalized associativity statement lem-trf-derived-pullback-coherence

proof.text:
Finally apply [lem-trf-derived-pullback-coherence] to $(j,h,k)=(r_X,s_X,u)$:
$$(P_{r_X}c_{s_X,u})c_{r_X,us_X}=(c_{r_X,s_X}P_u)c_{s_Xr_X,u}=(d_XP_u)c_{t_X,u}.$$
Thus step 4 becomes $H=(d_XP_u)c_{t_X,u}c_{u,t_Y}^{-1}=(d_XP_u)C_t$. By step 2 the transport between the last two factors is exactly that along $t_Yu=ut_X$ in the definition of $C_t$. This proves the required natural-transformation equality on all of $D_Y$. The functor associators here only reassociate evaluation of three functors, as in the cited coherence equation; no square is assumed Cartesian.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; agent pasting deduction from the normalized associativity statement lem-trf-derived-pullback-coherence

proof.text: For the representative clause, take any K-flat complex $K$ of $A_Y$-modules with flat terms. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], each successive ordinary module pullback in the displayed formulas is again K-flat with flat terms, applying that statement repeatedly to the ringed pro-etale topoi with their canonical coefficient maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], every component $c_{a,b}$ occurring here is the class of its canonical termwise module-pullback map on these complexes. Its inverse is represented by the inverse termwise isomorphism, since localization preserves inverse identities. The ordinary termwise pullback computes the derived pullback by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], so whiskering corresponds to applying that ordinary pullback to the termwise map. Equality transports also agree with termwise transports, by substitution (the reflexive equality gives identities in both constructions). Composing these maps gives precisely the two termwise pasting maps whose classes are the components of the two sides. This proves the claimed normalization without restricting $K$ to bounded complexes and without any flatness hypothesis on the scheme morphisms.
